html:
SMTO-PRX-0006 — Proxmox profile is invalid

GUID: 4ae0767e-36d6-4e58-ac15-0d980bee0162
Slug: proxmox-profile-invalid
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use the saved Proxmox Server details for this request. They changed after the request started, or something in them is missing or in the wrong form. SMTO stopped instead of guessing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you edited or deleted your Proxmox parameter after this request started, send your request again as a new message, mentioning the Proxmox parameter with @. A request keeps the exact copy of the details it started with, and SMTO won't swap in a newer copy partway through.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select your Proxmox parameter, open the Value tab and select Reveal & edit value. Check that "server" holds the server's name or address, "port" is a plain number such as 8006, and "scheme" is "https". SMTO refuses a Proxmox profile with an empty server, a port written in quotes, or a scheme other than https.
  3. In the same value, check that "username" includes its sign-in realm, for example root@pam, and that no extra fields were added. Then select Save. The Proxmox profile only accepts its own fields, and a username without the @realm part is rejected.
  4. If you asked about a specific node or VM, ask again using its exact name or ID number as Proxmox shows it. SMTO also stops when the node or VM part of the request is blank or contains odd characters.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reaches your Proxmox server and shows the VM list or status you asked for, without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Proxmox server. Don't keep sending the same request without fixing the saved details, and don't paste your Proxmox password into the chat.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Proxmox skill rejected the selected Proxmox Server parameter because its value failed server_connection validation or its accepted revision could not be restored, or because a guest path component (node, type or VMID) was empty, '.', '..' or contained control characters.

What this means

  • Accepted profile resolution/typed validation fails, its captured private revision is unavailable, or an endpoint path substitution is empty/unsafe. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • Accepted profile resolution/typed validation fails, its captured private revision is unavailable, or an endpoint path substitution is empty/unsafe.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish stale profile revision from invalid typed fields or path parameters.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the Proxmox Server record in Parameter Store: it must be a server_connection with service 'proxmox', scheme 'https', a non-empty server (at most 253 characters), an integer port from 1 to 65535, a boolean verify_tls, a username that is empty or matches user@realm, and no extra keys (validate_typed in agent_runtime/parameters/templates.py). If the record is valid, check the node and VMID values passed to expand_path in agent_runtime/skills/proxmox/client.py; do not substitute another profile or secret into an already accepted task.
  • Correct the identified profile/path field or explicitly capture an available intended profile revision; do not substitute another secret into an accepted task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The accepted current profile and exact path components validate for the intended server.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
